assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational body of political-economy research linking political institutions, state capacity, electoral incentives and fiscal policy to economic development and public policy.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini each made central, complementary contributions, though the field also has important adjacent contributors.
assessment.maturity: The theoretical and empirical agendas have shaped research and policy discussion for decades and are sufficiently mature for assessment.
uncertainties: The broad contribution combines several closely related strands, making a single prize formulation and boundary difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data research transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and made its geographic and policy correlates economically consequential.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are especially central to the mobility agenda, with Friedman an important collaborator in its empirical development.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been extensively developed across settings and have had unusually broad influence on research and public understanding.
uncertainties: Interpretation of descriptive mobility patterns as causal policy guidance remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work put exhaustible resources, natural capital and biodiversity at the center of rigorous intertemporal economic analysis.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are clearly associated with foundational resource-economics work, while inclusive wealth reflects a wider subsequent literature.
assessment.maturity: The intellectual contribution is long established and increasingly relevant as environmental constraints enter policy and national accounting.
uncertainties: The appropriate measurement and valuation of biodiversity and natural capital remain unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research gave compelling evidence that technology, tasks and trade shocks reshape local labour demand, earnings and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson constitute a coherent core for the trade-shock and task-based empirical contribution.
assessment.maturity: The research has generated a large follow-on literature and has materially changed analysis of globalization's distributional consequences.
uncertainties: The relative importance and external validity of trade, technology and institutional mechanisms vary across places and periods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence studies supplied influential and intelligible causal evidence on discrimination in labour markets and advanced audit-study methodology.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are central to the landmark field-experimental contribution; Charles is an important scholar in the broader topic.
assessment.maturity: The design has been replicated and extended widely, with durable influence on labour economics and discrimination research.
uncertainties: Audit-study estimates identify discrimination at particular stages of hiring and do not alone measure all mechanisms behind labour-market inequality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework sharpened quantitative analysis of why firms and countries differ so greatly in productivity and income.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia made closely linked contributions to measuring and modeling allocative distortions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established and influential in development, growth and firm-dynamics research.
uncertainties: Revenue-productivity measures can conflate genuine distortions with demand, markups, adjustment costs and measurement error.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life shocks and child health made the long-run formation of human capital central to applied microeconomics.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond are leading figures in the causal empirical literature; Cunha provides an important complementary skill-formation framework.
assessment.maturity: A broad body of quasi-experimental evidence has accumulated across cohorts, settings and outcomes.
uncertainties: Effect sizes and mechanisms may depend strongly on context, and translating shock evidence into intervention effects is not straightforward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their reconstruction of top incomes, wealth concentration and offshore wealth fundamentally expanded the empirical basis for studying inequality.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are core architects of the modern top-income series, with Zucman central to the offshore-wealth component.
assessment.maturity: The data infrastructure and research program have had major international influence and sustained scholarly uptake.
uncertainties: Top-tail estimates require consequential assumptions about tax avoidance, missing wealth and capitalization, and normative implications exceed the measurement results.
